summary: Proxy thread saturation during tenant affinity migration causing intermittent 503s and elevated error rate
description:
Issue summary:
During a staged tenant affinity migration (reassigning tenant session affinity to new proxy pools), we observed a correlated rise in 503 responses for a subset of dedicated customers. Error rate for affected route rose from baseline ~0.2% to 7% over a 12-minute window.

Impact:
- Several dedicated tenants (notably CacheCorp) reported intermittent 503s on generate and chat endpoints.
- Elevated customer error rate and increased p99 latency for small payload streaming sessions.
- No large-scale GPU OOMs, but upstream runtime processes recorded abnormal panics and worker restarts.

Environment:
- prod us-east (az: us-east-1a/us-east-1b)
- Rolling affinity migration job started at 2026-03-10T18:06:00Z

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Trigger affinity migration for a target tenant pool (internal migration job).
2) Proxy accept queue depth increases and ingress-proxy thread busy count climbs to 100% on a subset of nodes.
3) Apigw begins returning 503 to clients when hedged/streaming handshakes stall.
4) Upstream runtimes hit thread scheduling contention leading to SIGABRT in one runtime process, followed by immediate restarts.

Key logs / metrics observed:
- apigw.ingress.accept_queue.depth from 20 -> 900 within 6m for nodes handling migrated tenants.
- ingress-proxy.thread_pool.busy_pct -> 98% on 3/6 nodes.
- runtime.process[worker-12].panic: "sched_yield failed: thread-starve" (repeated 8 times)
- error-rate(route: /v1/chat/completions) spiked to 7% and gradually recovered after rollback.

Relevant runbook excerpt: "If ingress accept queue rises > 500 and 5xx rate > 1% for >5m, pause affinity job and investigate threadpool utilization."
comments: 2026-03-10 18:12 Support (Samira): Customer CacheCorp reporting intermittent 503s; provided sample request IDs and timestamps. Escalating to SRE.
2026-03-10 18:18 SRE (Ethan): Observed accept_queue depth spike correlated to affinity migration job. Marking incident Sev1 and pausing migration as immediate mitigation.

2026-03-10 18:22 Engineering (Priya Singh): Noted ingress-proxy thread_pool busy_pct near 100% on three proxy nodes. Increased proxy threadpool size on the fly for the affected nodes as stopgap. Monitoring impact.

2026-03-10 18:35 SRE (Ethan): After threadpool bump, error rate fell from 7% -> 2.5% over 10m but one runtime continued to crash repeatedly. Isolating tenant routing away from the problematic runtime node.
2026-03-10 19:00 SRE (Ethan): Rolled back affinity migration entirely per runbook. Error rate returned to baseline by 19:10 UTC. Notifying customer of temporary workarounds and rollback.
2026-03-11 09:15 Support (Samira): CacheCorp confirms service stabilized; requesting postmortem and preventative actions.

2026-03-12 14:00 Eng (Priya): Deployed proxy hotfix to improve accept-queue backpressure handling and a patch to the runtime scheduler to avoid panic on transient thread-starve. Scheduling controlled re-run of migration with throttling next week.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Hypothesis A: Affinity migration produced a short-lived connection-fanout that overfilled proxy accept queues and starved proxy thread workers. Evidence: accept_queue spike aligned exactly with migration window.
- Hypothesis B: Proxy threadpool configuration too conservative for concurrency shape of the migrated tenants; threadpool exhaustion cascaded to upstream hedged retries. Evidence: nodes hit 98-100% busy and immediate improvement after bumping pool size.
- Hypothesis C: Synthetic runtime bug: under heavy ingress scheduling pressure, runtime scheduler can hit an assert leading to panic. Evidence: single runtime binary showed repeated "sched_yield failed" panics. Related to an edge case in runtimes with pinned affinity.

Partial findings:
- No network-level packet loss detected; TCP retransmit rates stayed nominal.
- Proxy CPU was high but not saturated; contention was on thread availability and accept-queue handling.
- The runtime that crashed had been pinned to the same CPU affinity mask as the proxy process (legacy deploy config) — likely amplifying contention under the migration load.

Short-term mitigations applied:
- Paused the affinity migration job at 18:20 UTC.
- Increased ingress-proxy threadpool on affected nodes.
- Rerouted tenant traffic away from the offending runtime instance.
- Notified CacheCorp and tracked SLA impact metrics.

Longer-term action items (captured separately):
- Remove hard CPU affinity pinning between proxy and runtime in dedicated deploys (ENG-5741).
- Add migration-rate limiter to affinity job (OPS-1122).
- Improve proxy accept-queue observability and automated pause when depth > 400 (OBS-908).
- Runtime scheduler guard to avoid panic on transient thread-starve (RUNTIME-231).
resolution_notes:
Root cause summary:
A high-rate tenant affinity migration caused a concentrated burst of new accept handoffs on a subset of ingress-proxy nodes. The ingress-proxy threadpool was exhausted by the handoff pattern (accept_queue growth + busy threads). This amplified into upstream pressure: hedged retries and stalled handshakes increased runtime scheduling pressure and exposed a latent runtime panic when CPU affinity contention occurred.

Fix and rollout:
- Immediate: paused the affinity migration and increased proxy threadpool size on affected nodes. Rerouted traffic away from the unstable runtime.
- Hotfixes committed: proxy backpressure handling improvement (PR #1892) and runtime scheduler guard to prevent panic (PR #2145). Both were deployed to a canary subset on 2026-03-12 and monitored for 24h.
- Preventative: affinity migration job updated with rate limiting and pre-flight checks that verify accept_queue < 50 on target nodes. CPU affinity pins removed for proxy/runtime co-location in dedicated clusters.

Customer communication:
- Notified CacheCorp immediately after rollback and followed up with a technical summary and mitigation timeline. No billing adjustments requested; support credited 1 day of reduced SLA as goodwill.

Post-incident follow-up:
- Engineering to run a controlled re-run of tenant migrations with throttling on 2026-03-18 (ENG-6542).
- Observability: add alert for combined metric (accept_queue > 400 && 5xx_rate > 1% for 5m).
- Ops: update migration runbook to include preflight threadpool and affinity checks.

Status: Resolved (hotfix deployed + migration paused and policies updated).
